India's decision to leave out fast bowler Mohammed Siraj from the playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand has triggered a debate that has gone well beyond cricket. While former cricketers have questioned the team management's decision on sporting grounds, a Congress leader alleged that Siraj was dropped because of his religion. The BJP strongly rejected the charge, accusing the opposition of bringing communal politics into cricket. Samah Qundeel explains what is the controversy about.
